_comment_file: The application settings screen and its six sections. Loaded when the screen opens, not before. Section titles double as the navigation labels, so they stay short; the descriptions underneath carry the explanation.

screen.title: Settings
screen._comment_closeHint: Esc is a key name and is not translated.
screen.loadFailed: Your settings could not be read.

appearance.title: Theme
appearance.description: A theme is a token override file. The high-contrast pair meets WCAG 2.2 AA at every size, not only for body text.
appearance._comment_systemNow: {resolved} is systemLight or systemDark below, so the whole sentence is one message rather than two halves joined at run time.
appearance.terminalNote: The terminal has its own colours and font, on the Terminal tab: eight palettes, per-colour editing and a contrast check. Its palette follows the theme you pick here until you choose one there.

language.title: Language
language.description: Ten languages are planned for 1.0. Right-to-left languages mirror the whole layout, not just the text.
language._comment_progress: PLURAL, on the number of languages that actually have catalogues. The count is measured from the locales/ directory rather than hardcoded, so this sentence stops claiming 'only English' the day a second catalogue lands.
language.progress: {available, plural, one {Only English is translated so far.} other {# languages are translated so far.}} The rest are listed because translation is under way; each becomes selectable when its catalogue is complete, and until then choosing it would change nothing.
language._comment_unavailableLabel: The accessible name of a row that cannot be chosen. {name} is the language's own name, in its own script, and is never translated.
language._comment_rtl: A badge on right-to-left languages. Abbreviation; expand it if the language has no equivalent short form.
language._comment_storedUnavailable: Shown when the settings file names a language with no catalogue — a downgrade, or a translation withdrawn. {locale} is a BCP 47 tag such as pt-BR and is not translated.
language.storedUnavailable: Your settings ask for {locale}, which has no catalogue yet, so the interface stays in English.

terminal.paletteDescription: The colours every session in this window is drawn in. Separate from the interface theme, so a light interface can have a dark terminal. Changes reach sessions that are already open — nothing needs reconnecting.
terminal.autoCredit: Remoter Dark with a dark interface, Remoter Light with a light one, and the high-contrast palette when the interface is high contrast
terminal._comment_autoResolved: {name} is a palette name such as 'Remoter Dark'. Palette names are product names and are not translated.
terminal.previewNote: Real output, in the palette and font about to be applied.
terminal.contrastDescription: Every colour a program prints text in, measured against your background. WCAG 2.2 AA asks for 4.5:1 at this size. Nothing here is blocked — it is your terminal — but these are the colours that will be hard to read.
terminal.contrastClear: Every colour clears 4.5:1 against this background.
terminal._comment_contrastSample: The two letters drawn in each failing colour, as a specimen. Replace them with characters representative of the script this locale is read in — the point is to show what that colour looks like as text a reader would actually meet. Keep it to two or three characters.
terminal._comment_contrastRatio: A contrast ratio, already formatted to one decimal by Intl. The ':1' is notation, not words.
terminal._comment_contrastCount: PLURAL. 4.5:1 is a WCAG threshold and stays a numeral in every language.
terminal.contrastCount: {count, plural, one {# colour falls below 4.5:1} other {# colours fall below 4.5:1}}
terminal.contrastWarning: Change the colour, change the background, or leave it as it is — this is a measurement, not a refusal.
terminal.contrastBlacks: Colour 0 and colour 8 are the two a shell normally uses as a background or as dimmed decoration rather than as text, which is why they fall short in almost every palette ever published, including this one.
terminal._comment_colours: What each editable colour is called, in the order the editor lists them. The leading number is the ANSI colour index and stays a numeral; the word after it is translated. 'Bright black' is the conventional name for ANSI 8 even though it is usually dark grey — keep the convention rather than describing the colour.
terminal.coloursDescription: Pick a colour, or paste a hex value — #rgb, #rrggbb and #rrggbbaa are all accepted. A colour you have changed shows a reset beside it. The platform's colour picker has no transparency, so a colour that had some keeps it; the hex field, as #rrggbbaa, is where transparency is changed.
terminal._comment_hexLabel: {name} is a colour's name, such as 'Red' or 'Bright black'. These are the ANSI colour names and are translated.
terminal.resetOne: Reset {name} to the palette's own colour
terminal.overriddenCount: {count, plural, one {# colour differs from the palette} other {# colours differ from the palette}}
terminal.invalidHex: That is not a colour. Write it as #1a1c20.
terminal.fontDescription: Separate from the interface font. The interface stays at its own size when you change this.
terminal.fontFamilyHelp: The name of a font installed on this machine. Remoter cannot list the fonts you have, and it cannot tell you whether this one was found — the preview above is set in it, so an empty-looking change means the name did not match. Whatever you type falls back to the interface's monospace stack, so a typo never leaves you without a monospace terminal.
terminal.fontFamilyDefault: Leave it empty to use the interface's monospace stack.
terminal._comment_fontSizeHelp: {min} and {max} are the bounds the build enforces, so the sentence cannot drift out of step with the control.
terminal.fontSizeHelp: Pixels, {min} to {max}. The session resizes itself and tells the remote host the new geometry.
terminal.scope: These settings belong to this machine, not to the vault, and they apply to every session rather than to one connection.
terminal.saveFailed: The terminal appearance was not saved.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
shortcuts.description: Every binding below is what the application actually listens for. A focused terminal must receive almost every keystroke, so application shortcuts inside a session go through a prefix.
shortcuts.loadFailed: Your shortcut map could not be read.
shortcuts.loadFallback: These are the shipped defaults. Any binding you changed is not shown, and cannot be changed here until the settings file can be read.
shortcuts._comment_prefixBody: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D and Alt+F are key names. Translate the sentence, not the keys.
shortcuts.prefixBody: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D and Alt+F belong to the remote host, so Remoter does not take them. Inside a session, hold the prefix as well.
shortcuts.prefixLegend: The prefix held with an application shortcut inside a session
shortcuts.caption: Keyboard shortcuts, with what each one can and cannot reach
shortcuts._comment_inSession: {keys} is a key combination such as 'Ctrl+B then T'. Key names are not translated.
shortcuts.capturingHint: Press the combination you want, or Esc to cancel.
shortcuts.fixed: The shortcut for {action} cannot be changed
shortcuts.resetAllNone: Every editable shortcut is already at its shipped default.
shortcuts._comment_count: PLURAL on {shown}, with {total} inside it. Filtering a table down to one row is common enough that the singular is worth having.
shortcuts.count: {shown, plural, one {Showing # of {total} shortcuts.} other {Showing # of {total} shortcuts.}}
shortcuts._comment_conflictDuplicate: {holders} is a locale-joined list of action names, built with Intl.ListFormat.
shortcuts.conflictDuplicate: Already held by {holders}. Only one of them can fire, so change one of the two.
shortcuts.conflictReservedUniversal: The remote shell needs these keys, so a focused session keeps them and this shortcut never fires there.
shortcuts.conflictReservedApplication: These keys belong to the remote shell and to copy-and-paste. The prefix keeps them clear inside a session, but outside one Remoter takes them.
shortcuts.conflictDesktop: Some desktops take this combination for their own window switcher and win. Where that happens the press never reaches Remoter.
shortcuts.refusedInvalid: That is not a combination Remoter can bind.
shortcuts.refusedReserved: {keys} belongs to the remote host: a focused terminal has to receive it, so binding it here would stop it reaching the shell.
shortcuts.refusedDuplicate: {keys} is already held by {action}. Nothing was changed — free it there first, or pick another combination.
shortcuts.refusedUnknown: This build does not carry that action.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: Remoter can look for a newer release. It does not install one, and it contacts nothing unless you ask it to.
updates.switchLabel: Look for a newer release automatically
updates._comment_consent: SECURITY-CRITICAL. This is the consent notice for the only outbound request the application makes. Every clause is a commitment: what is contacted, how often, and exactly what is sent. Do not shorten it, and do not generalise 'one thing: this build's version string' into 'some information'.
updates.consent: With this on, Remoter contacts github.com at most once a day — once when you turn it on, and after that when you open this screen — and sends one thing: this build's version string. No identifier, no locale, no telemetry, no usage data. With it off, nothing is contacted until you press Check now.
updates.checking: Asking GitHub what has been released…
updates._comment_lastChecked: {when} is a relative time from Intl.RelativeTimeFormat — 'yesterday', '3 hours ago'.
updates.checkFailed: The update check did not finish.
updates._comment_current: {version} here and in the three messages below is a version string such as 0.1.0. Never translated, and never localised as a number — 0.1.0 does not become 0,1,0.
updates.current: You are running {version}, and it is the newest release.
updates.none: No release has been published yet. You are running {version}.
updates.unknown: This build reports its version as {version}, which is not a version that can be compared. Open the releases page and check by eye.
updates.notesNone: This release was published without notes.
updates._comment_noSelfUpdate: SECURITY-CRITICAL. It states why the application will not install its own updates. Keep the reason — unsigned releases — rather than reducing it to 'for safety'.
updates.noSelfUpdate: Remoter does not install updates itself. Releases are not signed yet, and running an unsigned binary is not something a credential manager should ask you to do — so the button opens the release page in your browser and you install it yourself.
updates.openFailed: The system browser did not open.
updates._comment_promiseTelemetry: SECURITY-CRITICAL, as are the two promises after it. Three absolute statements about what the application does not do. A translator who hedges any of them turns a commitment into marketing.
updates.promiseTelemetry: No telemetry. No usage reporting. No analytics of any kind, at any setting.
updates.promiseCrash: No crash upload. A crash report is written to your machine and you decide whether to attach it to an issue — which means you can read it first, and that matters when the process holds credentials.
updates.promiseCheck: The update check is the only request Remoter makes that is not a session you opened. It reads the public release list and sends this build's version. It downloads nothing.

about.title: About
about.description: What this build is, and the terms it is under.
about._comment_licenceValue: The licence's own name and SPDX identifier. Not translated: it is the legal name of the document.
about.licenceValue: GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later)
about.exceptionValue: This build cannot load plugins. There is no plugin host in it yet — only the ABI the future one will use. When there is: a WebAssembly plugin that talks to Remoter only through the published plugin ABI may be licensed on any terms you choose, which is the interface exception in LICENSE-EXCEPTION.
about.updatesValue: Remoter checks for a newer release only if you turn the check on, and it never installs one. See the Updates section.
about.repositoryFailed: The system browser did not open.
